title: Protection of Ports Special Measures Act 1948

sections.shortTitle: Protection of Ports Special Measures Act 1948
sections.description:
Short title extent and commencement

THE PROTECTION OF PORTS (SPECIAL MEASURES) ACT, 1948
THE PROTECTION OF PORTS (SPECIAL MEASURES) ACT, 1948
ACT No. XVII of 1948
(For
Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gaz. of P., 1948, Pt. V, p. 121.)
[11th June, 1948]
An Act to provide for special measures to ensure the
protection of ports
WHEREAS it is
necessary to provide for special measures to ensure the protection of ports;
It is hereby
enacted as follows:-
1. Short title extent and commencement.-(1) This Act may be called the Protection of Ports (Special
Measures) Act, 1948.
(2) It shall
extend to the Port of Chittagong in the first instance, but may at any time, by
notification in the official Gazette, be extended by the Central Government to
any other port in (The original words "the Dominion of" omitted by A.
O., 1961, Art. 2 and Sch. (with effect from the 23rd March, 1956).)* * * Pakistan.
(3) It shall
come into force at once.

Interpretation

THE PROTECTION OF PORTS (SPECIAL MEASURES) ACT, 1948
THE PROTECTION OF PORTS (SPECIAL MEASURES) ACT, 1948
ACT No. XVII of 1948
(For
Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gaz. of P., 1948, Pt. V, p. 121.)
[11th June, 1948]
An Act to provide for special measures to ensure the
protection of ports
WHEREAS it is
necessary to provide for special measures to ensure the protection of ports;
2. Interpretation. In this
Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,-
(a)
"port" means a "major port" as defined in sub-section (8)
of section 3 of the Ports Act, 1908, XV of 1908;
(b)
"protected area" means an area declared to be a protected area under
the next succeeding sec tion.

sections.shortTitle: Protection of Ports Special Measures Act 1948
sections.description:
Protected areas

THE PROTECTION OF PORTS (SPECIAL MEASURES) ACT, 1948
THE PROTECTION OF PORTS (SPECIAL MEASURES) ACT, 1948
ACT No. XVII of 1948
(For
Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gaz. of P., 1948, Pt. V, p. 121.)
[11th June, 1948]
An Act to provide for special measures to ensure the
protection of ports
WHEREAS it is
necessary to provide for special measures to ensure the protection of ports;
3. Protected areas.-(1) If
the Central Government considers it necessary or expedient to regulate the
entry of persons into a port, it may, by notified order, declare the port to be
a protected area, and thereupon, for so long as the order is in force, such
area shall be a protected area for the purposes of this Act.
(2) A
notification under sub-section (1) shall define the limits of the area to which
it refers:
Provided that
the Central Government may alter such limits from time to time by a
notification issued in this behalf.
(3) Limits
defined under sub-section (2) may include any piers, jetties, landing-places,
wharves, quays, docks and other works made on behalf of the public for
convenience of traffic, for safety of vessels, or for the improvement,
maintenance or good government of the port and its approaches, whether within
or without high-watermark, and any portion of the shore or bank within any
limits considered necessary by Government.

sections.shortTitle: Protection of Ports Special Measures Act 1948
sections.description:
Rules for regulation of entry, etc.

THE PROTECTION OF PORTS (SPECIAL MEASURES) ACT, 1948
THE PROTECTION OF PORTS (SPECIAL MEASURES) ACT, 1948
ACT No. XVII of 1948
(For
Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gaz. of P., 1948, Pt. V, p. 121.)
[11th June, 1948]
An Act to provide for special measures to ensure the
protection of ports
WHEREAS it is
necessary to provide for special measures to ensure the protection of ports;
4. Rules for regulation of entry, etc.,-(1) The Central Government may, by notification in the official
Gazette, make Rules for controlling or regulating e the admission of persons
to, and the conduct of persons in, and in the vicinity of, a protected area.
(2) In
particular, and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, the
Central Government may make Rules for any or all of the following purposes,
namely:
(a) for
restricting the entry of persons into the pro tected area;
(b) for removing
persons from the protected area;
(c) for dealing
with persons loitering in suspicious circumstances in the vicinity of the
protected area.

6. Penalties. Whoever
contravenes any Rule made under this Act or an order passed in pursuance
thereof shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three
years or with fine, or with both.
sections.punishment:
punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three
years or with fine, or with both.

Saving of other laws

THE PROTECTION OF PORTS (SPECIAL MEASURES) ACT, 1948
THE PROTECTION OF PORTS (SPECIAL MEASURES) ACT, 1948
ACT No. XVII of 1948
(For
Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gaz. of P., 1948, Pt. V, p. 121.)
[11th June, 1948]
An Act to provide for special measures to ensure the
protection of ports
WHEREAS it is
necessary to provide for special measures to ensure the protection of ports;
9. Saving of other laws.
The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to and not in derogation of any
other law for the time being in force regulating the admission of persons to,
and the conduct of persons in, and in the vicinity of, a port.
